subject: Day 66: set a sleep-onset routine
bodyText:
Today's focus
Sleep is near its most predictable in the 8-to-14-week window, so this is the week to chain a fixed wind-down. A repeatable sequence becomes the cue that tells Avi sleep is next.

Action items
- Lock in a fixed three-step wind-down tonight (bath, then one book, then a lights-out song) in the same order every evening; a consistent sequence builds the sleep-onset association that anchors as his pattern stabilizes by 12 to 14 weeks. AAP HealthyChildren: getting your baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Note last wake time, time he fell asleep, and nap length for the next several days so you can see his emerging wake windows before committing to clock times. AAP HealthyChildren: baby sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Aim the last nap to end by 16:30 to 17:00 so bedtime can land around 18:30 to 19:30 without overtiredness amplifying night wakings.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Non-painful spit-up after feeds, decreasing in volume as the upper esophageal sphincter matures.
- [monitor] No reliable social smile by now; document it and flag it at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] A new persistent crying pattern or a feeding refusal that runs more than 24 hours.
- [call now] Rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, apnea, seizure-like activity, or blue lips with labored breathing. Call 911 for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Chain bath, book, and the lights-out song into one fixed nightly sequence; the predictability itself is what trains sleep onset as his rhythm consolidates by 12 to 14 weeks. AAP HealthyChildren: getting your baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Read the same calm wind-down book at the same point each night; the repeated prosody becomes a recognizable signal and seeds early literacy at the same time. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Track last wake, fall-asleep time, and nap length across a few days to surface his natural windows before you try to anchor a loose schedule. AAP HealthyChildren: baby sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 84-91: sleep-consolidation window opens around 3 months; the routine you set this week becomes the backbone of it.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit and vaccines (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).
- Around week 14-18: the 4-month sleep regression is on the horizon, after which a sturdy wind-down routine pays off most.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Smiles on his own to get your attention
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Initiates the smile rather than responding to yours — emerging social agency.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/smiles-to-get-attention/complete

- Chuckles (not yet a full laugh)
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Throaty soft laugh sounds. Precedes the full belly laugh by a few weeks.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/chuckles/complete

- Turns head toward the sound of your voice
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Localizes sound source. Worth raising with the pediatrician if absent at the 4-month visit.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/turns-head-toward-sound/complete

- Makes sounds back when you talk to him
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Conversational turn-taking. Foundation for later vocabulary growth.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/makes-sounds-back/complete

- Opens mouth when she sees the breast or bottle
  AAP window: day 60-120
  What to look for: Anticipatory recognition — feeding is now associated with the sight, not just the sensation.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/opens-mouth-for-breast/complete
